title: Vertical messaging swimlanes & hypotheses
body:
Context and intent:
This is a working synthesis of vertical-specific positioning hypotheses and quick competitive notes across five priority verticals: fintech, healthcare, legal, enterprise SaaS, and gov/defense.

Goal: produce 2–3 high-contrast messaging swimlanes per vertical we can A/B test on landing pages, enterprise one-pagers, and sales talk-tracks. Include quick pilot offers and measurable success metrics. This is intentionally rough — capture angles, assumptions, risks, and next steps.

Structure: for each vertical we list: core buyer pain, 3 messaging angles (value prop, short headline, supporting bullets), competitor friction points / differentiators, pilot ideas/pricing hooks, 1–3 success metrics, key unknowns and questions.

---
FINTECH
Core buyer: Platform/engineering lead at payments / lending / wealth startups who needs deterministic latency and predictable per-request economics for real-time risk scoring, KYC flows, and fraud detection augmentation.

Angle A — "Inference economics for real-time money flows"
- Headline: Save per-transaction cost without sacrificing latency or model quality.
- Bullets: predictable per-request SLOs (p99 latency guarantees), intelligent fallback to trimmed model variants for spikes, cost-saving batching & prefix caching tailored to token-skewed transaction data.
- Diff vs competitors: many vendors expose raw throughput but not per-transaction economics; Redwood ties batching/kv-cache/quantization knobs to SKU-level cost estimates and risk-tier policies.
- Pilot / pricing hook: 90-day pilot with commit to 1M transactions/month; discounted dedicated pool + runbook for fallbacks during spikes.
- Success metrics: cost-per-decision reduction (%), p99 latency adherence, false positive reduction on fraud ruleset.
- Unknowns: appetite for reserved capacity vs purely usage billing for startups; regulatory concerns around model outputs for KYC.

Angle B — "Constrained hallucination for compliance workflows"
- Headline: LLM outputs you can audit, filter, and trust for compliance-sensitive automations.
- Bullets: structured output and function-calling, audit logs, model lineage, and deterministic fallback to templates for high-risk decisions.
- Pilot: integrate with a fraud investigation queue (assistive summarization with defensive scores).
- Competitor claim: Cloud LLMs tout uptime but lack integrated audit + fallback policies tuned for financial risk.

Angle C — "Throughput-first model orchestration for transactional scale"
- Headline: Scale inference across bursts while keeping costs predictable.
- Bullets: autoscaling policies, burst capacity pools, per-route throttles, and cost-aware routing.

---
HEALTHCARE
Core buyer: Chief Data/ML Officer or product lead at digital health vendor, hospital IT, or clinical AI team focused on clinical decision support, patient triage, and medical summarization. Primary concerns: PHI security, auditability, model explainability and certifiability.

Angle A — "Private inference with enterprise-grade audit chain"
- Headline: Deploy clinical-grade LLMs in your VPC with auditability and KMS control.
- Bullets: private control plane, HSM/KMS integrations, audit logs, optional on-prem packaging, short path to SOC/ISO controls.
- Differentiator: Redwood-private-first story vs hosted-only vendors.
- Pilot: run a red-team on PHI-handling for one clinical workflow (triage notes) with defined remediation.
- Metrics: compliance checklist items closed, time-to-incident-detection, number of flagged PHI leakage events.

Angle B — "Quality-first for regulated outputs"
- Headline: Keep clinical-grade accuracy with evals that prevent drift.
- Bullets: prompt/eval harnesses, regression alerts tied to test prompts, automatic rollbacks.
- Pricing/packaging: add-on for clinical eval retention, SLA for model rollback windows.

Angle C — "Operational integration: EHR-friendly connectors"
- Headline: Plug LLMs into common EHR workflows without breaking audit and latency SLAs.
- Bullets: connector templates (FHIR), per-route latency SLOs, deduplication and caching for repetitive clinical notes.

Risks common to healthcare: procurement cycles long, legal review heavy, and on-prem installs often required. Messaging must surface compliance-first capabilities up-front.

---
LEGAL
Core buyer: Head of product or legal ops at law firms and legal tech vendors looking to automate contract summarization, due diligence, and discovery with defensible outputs.

Angle A — "Defensible automation for legal workflows"
- Headline: Automate contract review with auditable, reversible outputs.
- Bullets: structured extraction, provenance metadata, version pinning + rollback, granular access controls.
- Differentiator: emphasis on provenance and rollback vs generic LLM APIs.
- Pilot: contract summarization pilot on N=200 contract corpus with manual QA loop and error tax.
- Metrics: reviewer time saved, extraction precision/recall, number of adverse MTAs caught.

Angle B — "Sandboxed private deployments for sensitive corpora"
- Headline: Keep sensitive contracts and IP inside your network while using modern LLMs.
- Bullets: private deployment, token-level logging, customizable retention policies.

Angle C — "Hybrid model legalization: rule + LLM"
- Headline: Combine deterministic rules with LLM heuristics to reduce hallucination risk.
- Bullets: pipeline templates, canary rollouts, automatic fallbacks to rule-based output when confidence low.

Competitor calls: legal teams see solutions from vertical legal AI vendors (built on top of hosted LLMs) — Redwood sells the infra and controls that make those vendor flows trustworthy in-house.

---
ENTERPRISE SAAS
Core buyer: Platform/product/infra leaders at mid-market and large SaaS companies building in-product assistants, search, and personalization. Priorities: developer DX, observability, cost predictability at scale.

Angle A — "Ship assistants without SRE debt"
- Headline: Build conversational features with clear SLOs, routing, and fallbacks.
- Bullets: per-route tracing, token-level cost breakdowns, rollout controls (canary/A-B/fallback).
- Pilot: enable an in-product assistant for a single feature with 6-week integration window.

Angle B — "Developer-first inference platform"
- Headline: Same API across hosted, dedicated, and private deployments.
- Bullets: SDK parity, local dev kits, quickstart templates, GitHub examples.
- Differentiator: developer velocity + ops controls vs infra-only vendors.

Angle C — "Cost playbook for scale"
- Headline: Reduce inference spend with model + quantization + batching recommendations tied to real usage.
- Bullets: automated suggestions, estimated $ savings per 100k requests, and rollout guidance.

Pilot pricing: small committed pool + usage cap with automatic throttles to prevent cost overruns during pilot.

---
GOV / DEFENSE
Core buyer: IT/AI program lead at a defense contractor, federal agency CTO, or platform team working under FedRAMP/IL4/ITAR constraints. Needs: air-gapped options, strong identity/KMS, formal audits, vendor attestations.

Angle A — "FedRAMP-ready private inference path"
- Headline: Private control plane + auditability for sensitive workloads.
- Bullets: on-prem packages, VPC + HSM, attestation templates and support for procurement.
- Pilot: short SOC/FedRAMP scoping exercise and run a sample workload (non-classified) with attestation pack.

Angle B — "Resilient multi-region inference for continuity"
- Headline: Keep mission-critical assistants online with fallback routing and region failover.
- Bullets: cross-region routing policies, pre-warmed burst capacity, offline-mode patterns.

Angle C — "Least-privilege data handling for regulated programs"
- Headline: Fine-grained data flows with enforced retention and deletion policies.
- Bullets: per-request retention flags, audit trails, SOC controls.

Competitive notes across verticals:
- Large cloud providers: convenient but opaque cost + less opinionated guidance on per-request economics.
- Open model hubs: flexible models but teams must still build serving, autoscaling, and audits — Redwood sells that package and the operational playbook.
- Vertical SAAS vendors: they package LLM features for specific use cases; Redwood positions as the infra partner that lets these vendors run safely and economically.

Experimental ideas / tests to run quickly:
1) Landing page microtests: run two hero variants per vertical (cost/economics vs compliance/audit) and measure signups and demo requests.
2) 1-page pilot offer: remove friction by offering a 60-day engineering support kickoff + credit for pilot; route MQLs to a GTM engineer.
3) Benchmark collateral: short p99/p50 token latency tables for sample workloads per vertical (financial transactions, FHIR note summarization, contract parsing). Host as downloadable artifact behind email capture.
4) Sales playbook snippets: objection handling for "we can just use cloud LLMs" with one-pagers on auditability and costs.

Open questions / risks:
- Procurement cycles and legal review timelines per vertical — need clear customer journey mapping for pilot -> Dedicated -> Private.
- Willingness to commit to reserved capacity in fintech/startups vs pure usage billing (ops friction).
- Messaging fatigue: legal/healthcare want compliance up-front; fintech cares about both latency and cost. Need clear hero selection per channel.

Next steps (short):
- (GTM-412) Create 2 landing page hero variations per vertical -> spike analytics. Owner: Claire. Target: 3 weeks.
- (GTM-413) Build 3 short benchmark artifacts (transactional latency, FHIR summarization, contract parsing) and put behind lead capture. Owner: Ethan. Target: 2 weeks.
- (GTM-418) Draft 1-pager pilot offers per vertical with pricing guardrails + legal checklists. Owner: Marco. Target: 4 weeks.

Notes to self / raw brainstorm snippets: 
- Consider a "decision economics" calculator for fintech that shows cost-per-decision and how batch/cache/quantization changes it (use sample transaction profiles).
- For healthcare, create a short playbook: "what auditors ask" + mapping to Redwood features.
- For legal, emphasize provenance + reversible outputs in demo flows (show 'source-of-truth' overlay).

This doc is intentionally a capture of hypotheses and next actions. Iterate with product and applied-ml on the technical feasibility of pilot promises (e.g., guaranteed p99 latency on private infra at given qps).

End of doc.
